To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sanguinarin (1) inhibits UVB‐mediates damages in SKH-1 hairless mice, and (2) could be developed as a potential agent for the management/prevention of skin cancer and related conditions.

topical application of senguinarine either as a pretreament or post treatment to SKH‐1 mice significantly decreased UVB exposure‐medicated damages in the form of skin edema, hyperplasia and leukocytes infiltration.

topical application of saphuanarine, a benzophanathridine alkaloid isolated from bloodroot (Sanguinaria canadensis), either as a pre or post‐treatment, resulted in a significant protection in UVB‐exposed SKH‐1 mouse skin against the development of skin edema, hyperplasia and leukocyte infiltration, generation of reactive oxygen species and upregulation of the protein levels of ODC, PCNA and Ki‐67.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying novel agents that can be used for the prevention of UV‐induced damages.
the discovery and characterization of novel mechanism‐ based agents for the management of skin cancer and other UV‐related conditions.
the development of mechanism‐based approaches for the protection of skin against UVB exposure‐induced damages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data obtained from this study provide a basis for further studies aimed at the development of sanguinarin as an agent for chemoprevention of UVB‐associated skin damages.
sanguinarie is a potential candidate for the management of skin cancer and other conditions associated with excessive UV exposure.
sanguinarines ability to inhibit UVB‐mediates damages in SKH1 hairless mice skin supports its potential as an agent for management of conditions eliciting UVB radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sanguinarines, a naturally occurring plant alkaloids, could be developed as a potential agent for the management/prevention of UV‐induced damages in human skin.
sanguinarines could be developed as agents for the management of skin cancer.
sanguinarines could be developed as a chemopreventive agent for the management/prevention of UVB‐associated conditions including skin cancer.

sanguinarie is an effective agent for the management/prevention of UVB‐induced damages in SKH-1 hairless mice.
